Thanks for the demo last week. Our legal and privacy teams have a short RFI focused on how Redwood handles controller vs processor scenarios, and how DPA annexes reflect routing for cross-border processing (especially transfers to the US). Markus is copied for legal detail.

High-level questions:
1) In customer deployments where VitaHealth is the data controller, do you (Redwood) act as a processor for model inference and logs? Which services are considered controller-facing vs processor-facing?
2) How are cross-border transfers handled when a customer pins a model variant hosted in the US but has EU data subjects? Describe available safeguards and where customer controls sit (routing, residency pinning, KMS).
3) Can you provide a DPA annex example showing subprocessors, export mechanisms, SCCs/DPF references, and optional on-prem narrow-scope configurations?

We appreciate a short written response and any annex draft you can share. Ideally by EOD 15 Nov so our procurement can move the NDA/DPA forward.

Avery / Kim / Marissa,

Draft technical responses below — kept tight for the RFI. I attached a short diagram as an excel tab (sent with the final).

Q1 (processor role):
- For hosted Redwood API and Dedicated, Redwood acts as a processor when processing customer data for inference. Customer remains controller for customer data sent into the service.
- Controller-vs-processor split:
  * Controller responsibilities remain with the customer: dataset selection, deciding retention windows, and mapping lawful basis for processing.
  * Redwood responsibilities (processor): model inference, ephemeral KV caches, audit logging, and producing telemetry. We offer configuration options so customers can limit which telemetry leaves the tenancy.

Q2 (cross-border transfers / residency):
- Residency controls: customers can pin inference to region-specific pools (e.g., eu-west-1). We support routing policies that prefer in-region execution, and automatic fallback to nearest compatible region when capacity constraints occur.
- Safeguards: (i) standard contractual clauses (SCCs) + DPF references for EU-US transfers in our DPA annex, (ii) customer-managed KMS for key encryption of persistent artifacts, (iii) prefix/KV caching TTL controls to avoid persistent storage of EU personal data in non-EU regions.
- For EU data subjects where customer requires strictly EU processing, we offer Redwood Private (VPC or on-prem) which ensures no egress to US-hosted runtime.

Q3 (DPA annex example):
- Attached: redwood-dpa-annex-v1.pdf (template) — includes subprocessors list, SCCs adoption statement, and two optional operation modes: Hosted (with SCC + DPF fallback) and Private (VPC/on-prem, no cross-border).

Notes / open items for legal:
- Need Kim to review our SCC wording and confirm DPF phrasing (we reference DPF as a mitigation where SCCs apply).
- Recommend we include a short service-level statement for key material (KMS) ownership options.

I will compile the excel with the short network/flow diagram and token retention table and send back for Kim to finalize legal language.

—Ben

Thanks Ben — good draft. I made legal edits and prepared an annex template that calls out: subprocessors (hosting, monitoring, SSO providers), reliance on SCCs for EU-US transfers, optional DPF acknowledgement (we indicate Redwood "supports" DPF mechanisms but do not certify independent adequacy), and two operational modes (Hosted with SCCs + contractual safeguards; Private: no cross-border transfers).

Key proposed language:
- Subprocessor clause: we will notify customers 30 days prior to onboarding a new subprocessor and provide escalation rights for critical subprocessors.
- SCCs/DPF: include SCCs by reference and confirm Redwood will rely on SCCs for transfers; include a customer option to require KMS ownership (customer-managed keys) for persistent artifacts.
- Fallback routing: include a paragraph that in the event of region-level capacity constraints, Redwood will first attempt in-region alternatives, then notify the customer and only failover with prior approval or a pre-agreed policy.

I attached redwood-dpa-annex-v1.pdf with tracked changes and an answer spreadsheet with line-by-line RFI replies. Ben — please confirm the KMS wording aligns with product where we say "customer-managed keys available for Dedicated and Private".

-Kim
